risk_description: Data loss or state inconsistency due to 'Last Write Wins' conflict resolution strategy in offline-sync scenarios, particularly if a user modifies the same record (e.g., reading session) on multiple devices while offline.
root_cause: Adoption of a simplistic conflict resolution strategy ('Last Write Wins') for a complex multi-device sync requirement without field-level merging or user intervention logic.
mitigation_strategy: Implement server-side versioning (e.g., ETag/Timestamp checks) to detect conflicts rather than blindly overwriting. Implement a 'client-side backup' of local data before sync actions to allow recovery.
contingency_plan: Develop a manual conflict resolution UI for the mobile app to prompt users when server version > client version.
monitoring_trigger: High frequency of 'overwrite' events detected in sync logs or user reports of missing session data.

risk_description: App Store rejection (iOS) or Google Play policy violation regarding In-App Purchase (IAP) implementation or App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompts for AdMob.
root_cause: Strict and frequently changing platform guidelines regarding monetization flows, subscription disclosure, and user data tracking consent.
mitigation_strategy: Conduct a pre-submission review against Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and App Store Review Guidelines. Ensure the ATT prompt is displayed *before* AdMob initialization (WI-MOB-006). Implement robust receipt validation on the backend (WI-BE-003).
contingency_plan: Prepare toggle switches (Feature Flags) in the backend to remotely disable AdMob or specific IAP tiers if rejected, allowing a quick resubmission without a new binary.
monitoring_trigger: Rejection notice from App Store Review or crash reports initializing AdMob without consent.

risk_description: Cost overrun and latency spikes in AI Recommendation Service due to unoptimized Vector Search queries or high-volume usage of OpenAI API.
root_cause: OpenSearch Serverless and OpenAI API are pay-per-usage models; inefficient querying or lack of caching for frequent requests will drive up costs exponentially.
mitigation_strategy: Implement strict rate limiting per user tier (Free vs Premium) using Redis. Cache AI responses for identical contexts. Configure AWS Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts.
contingency_plan: Implement a 'circuit breaker' to switch to a simplified, non-AI recommendation algorithm (e.g., genre-based) if cost thresholds or latency SLAs are breached.
monitoring_trigger: Projected monthly spend exceeds budget by 15% or P95 latency for recommendations > 3s.

risk_description: Local database (Isar) schema corruption or data loss during mobile app updates if schema migrations are not handled perfectly.
root_cause: The offline-first architecture relies heavily on the local Isar database. Changes to the data model in future updates require complex migration logic on client devices.
mitigation_strategy: Develop a comprehensive suite of automated migration tests covering version N to N+1 scenarios. Implement a 'safe mode' that resets the local DB and pulls fresh data from the server if corruption is detected.
contingency_plan: Force a full re-sync from the backend if migration fails, acknowledging potential loss of unsynced offline data.
monitoring_trigger: Spike in crash reports related to Isar exceptions or database open failures immediately following a release.

risk_description: Backend P95 latency violating the < 200ms requirement due to Aurora Serverless v2 scaling lag or Fargate cold starts.
root_cause: Serverless infrastructure (Aurora v2, Fargate) can introduce latency during scale-out events or from zero-scale states if not provisioned with minimum capacities.
mitigation_strategy: Configure minimum ACUs for Aurora to prevent 'pause'. Set Fargate tasks to a minimum count > 0. Implement application-level caching (Redis) for read-heavy endpoints (Dashboard/Library).
contingency_plan: Vertical scaling of Fargate tasks or switching Aurora to provisioned instances if Serverless performance remains inconsistent.
monitoring_trigger: CloudWatch Alarm: 'P95 Latency > 200ms' firing consistently for > 15 minutes.

risk_description: GDPR compliance failure due to incomplete PII scrubbing across distributed systems (Aurora, Logs, S3 backups) during account deletion.
root_cause: Data is distributed across relational DB, vector DB (OpenSearch), and potentially logs. 'Right to Erasure' requires atomic deletion across all.
mitigation_strategy: Implement a centralized 'DeleteUser' saga/transaction that triggers deletion in all subsystems. Ensure structured logging explicitly masks PII. Enable S3 Object Lock only for Audit logs, not PII.
contingency_plan: Manual deletion runbook execution by Ops team within the 30-day GDPR window if automated jobs fail.
monitoring_trigger: Audit logs showing 'Deletion Failed' status or PII detected in log aggregation system.
